title: Year 12 Earth and Environmental Science Module 6 – Hazards
description: A fast-recall review of NSW Year 12 Earth and Environmental Science Module 6, organised by its three Inquiry Questions. Questions use short answers and avoid multi-step calculations or extended writing.
course: NSW Earth and Environmental Science Stage 6
author: Generated with Classroom Jeopardy Quiz Maker

categories.name: How and why do geological disasters occur?

questions.prompt: What sudden release of energy in Earth’s crust produces seismic waves?
What point inside Earth is the origin of an earthquake?
What point on Earth’s surface lies directly above an earthquake focus?
What large sea wave can be generated by sudden displacement of the seafloor?
What type of plate boundary commonly produces deep-focus earthquakes?
questions.answer: A convergent boundary. Accept: subduction zone.

questions.prompt: Which type of magma is usually more explosive: low-viscosity basaltic magma or high-viscosity silica-rich magma?
What fast-moving mixture of volcanic ash, rock and hot gas travels down a volcano?
What volcanic mudflow made of water, ash and debris is called?

categories.name: How do natural disasters affect the biosphere & atmosphere?

questions.prompt: What sphere includes all living organisms?
What sphere contains the gases surrounding Earth?
What volcanic material can blanket vegetation and reduce photosynthesis?
What gas released by large eruptions can form sulfate aerosols that cool climate temporarily?
Which 1991 volcanic eruption is commonly studied for its global atmospheric cooling effect?
What Australian weather system can produce intense coastal rainfall, strong winds and flooding?
What ecological process describes the gradual recovery of communities after a major disturbance?
What happens to habitat availability when a natural disaster destroys vegetation and shelter?

categories.name: How can technology predict & minimise disaster impacts?

questions.prompt: What instrument records ground motion from earthquakes?
What satellite-based system can measure slow ground deformation around volcanoes?
Monitoring emissions of which volcanic gas can help indicate changing magma activity?
What remote-sensing system uses radio waves to track rainfall and storms?
Can scientists currently predict the exact time and location of an earthquake reliably?
What system detects an earthquake after it starts and sends alerts before strong shaking arrives elsewhere?
What engineering approach can reduce earthquake damage by allowing a building to move relative to the ground?
What broad term means reducing the harmful effects of a natural hazard?

finalRound.prompt: What does a natural hazard become when it causes major damage, disruption or loss of life?
